subject: Solara Dedicated GPU allocation: memory-density vs throughput decision
content:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Singh <rajesh@solara.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Solara Dedicated GPU allocation: memory-density vs throughput decision

Hi Rajesh —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attached is a concise allocation frame that balances Solara's high-context retrieval workload (long sequences, large KV caches) against the need for predictable throughput for inference-on-demand. The two artifacts in the attachment are:
- solara_capacity_workbook.xlsx — workload profile, projection-based reserve sizing, and a few run-rate scenarios
- h100_a100_l4_perf_matrix.pdf — microbenchmarks we ran against your mixed query set (1–32k tokens) on H100, A100, and L4 variants

Summary (TL;DR):
- If Solara prioritizes latency for long-context summarization and large-scale KV cache reuse, H100-reserved slots with 80% of the pool in H100 (64GB) + small L4 burst lanes looks best for predictability.
- If cost-per-token and high concurrent short-chat throughput are the priority, a majority-A100 fleet (40GB) with L4 for non-sensitive short requests yields the lowest unit cost.
- L4 is a strong economic option for stateless short queries (<2k tokens) but performs poorly when KV cache hits and long contexts dominate.

Ask: can you confirm which of the two priorities matters most for Q1: (A) low-latency long-context inference (H100-first) or (B) cost-efficient high-concurrency short prompts (A100-first + L4)? Once you confirm, we will lock a reserve recommendation and an operational fallthrough plan (burst lanes, cache-tiering, and prewarming).

Notes on risk and fallback included in the workbook.

Attachments: [Attachment: solara_capacity_workbook.xlsx (spreadsheet, 420KB)], [Attachment: h100_a100_l4_perf_matrix.pdf (pdf, 180KB)]

Best,
Mina Haddad

Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 15:18:42 -0800
Subject: Re: Solara Dedicated GPU allocation: memory-density vs throughput decision

Mina —

Appreciate the clear summary and the workbook. We have two competing priorities inside the product org:
1) The flagship "Summarize+Search" pipeline (high context, must keep KV cache warm) — product says H100-like behavior is ideal.
2) The in-app assistant for customer support (lots of short, concurrent calls) — finance will push for the cheaper option.

Procurement flagged budget constraints for Q1; they asked whether a blended reserve that starts A100-heavy with H100 headroom (or on-call H100 slots) is feasible. Also asked for an ops-level runbook for cache warmup and cross-SKU fallback.

Can you propose a blended path that reduces up-front reserve cost but preserves QoS for the Summarize+Search pipeline?

Thanks,
Rajesh
Head of Platforms | Solara AI
rajesh@solara.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Solara Dedicated GPU allocation: memory-density vs throughput decision

Mina / Karthik —

Quick internal note after reviewing the workbook and Rajesh's ask. I sketched a low-risk blended path that we can present to Procurement:

1) Phase 0 (pilot, 6 weeks): Reserve a small H100 pool sized to 10–15% of projected peak long-context traffic (prewarmed, pinned instances) + A100 pool for baseline inference. This limits initial commit while giving Summarize+Search an SLA-backed lane for critical requests.

2) Phase 1 (Q1 scale): Based on telemetry from the pilot (cache-hit rates and actual token distribution), expand H100 to ~35–45% and keep A100 at ~45–55%, with categorical routing rules: long-context and KV-affine queries go to H100; short, non-sensitive queries go to L4 burst lanes first.

3) Ops controls and fallbacks:
   - Cache-aware routing: maintain a tagging layer so requests include estimated KV size; runtime routes accordingly.
   - Prewarming windows: schedule H100 prewarm for expected peak 30 minutes prior (auto-scaler trigger).
   - Cross-sku fallback: when H100 capacity is exhausted, route lower-priority long-context requests to an A100 variant with reduced context (truncate or summarized preface) and fall back to L4 only for best-effort short responses.

4) Financial guardrails: commit to a 12-month convertible reserve that lets Solara swap slots between SKUs at quarterly checkpoints (we can include a step-down pricing concession if they move into a longer-term commit).

Attachment: I exported a short ops-runbook stub into the workbook under the "Pilot Runbook" tab.

If the group likes this framing, Mina — can you capture this as a consolidated slide (one-pager + ops appendix) for Procurement? I'll prepare the technical appendix for runtime routing and KV-tag examples.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Solara Dedicated GPU allocation: memory-density vs throughput decision

Rajesh / Procurement —

Thanks for the signal. Based on Dev's pilot-first framing, here's our proposal in simple terms you can take to Finance/Procurement:

Proposal (one-pager summary):
- Start: 3-month pilot with a small H100 reserve (12% of projected peak) + A100 baseline (60%) + L4 burst for non-sensitive low-context traffic (28%). Estimated monthly commit delta vs all-A100 is ~+18% for the pilot period.
- Why this helps: the pilot ensures Summarize+Search has an SLA-backed lane and gives enough telemetry to avoid overprovisioning H100 at commit.
- Fallthrough: A100 will serve degraded long-context responses if H100 saturates (with automated context-compression). L4 will not be used for long-context at any point unless explicitly configured.
- Ops & Pricing: we will ship a pilot runbook and routing rules. For a 12-month convertable reserve we can include a 10% discount on incremental H100 expansion if Solara commits within Q2.

Next steps:
1) Rajesh: confirm you can approve a 3-month pilot budget (Procurement prefers a number; see workbook tab "Pilot Cost" for the estimate)
2) Procurement: we will draft a short addendum for a convertible-reserve clause and the prewarm SLA
3) Dev / Karthik: can you both add the routing tag examples and prewarm SLO text to the shared Drive doc by EOD Wednesday?

If this all looks good I'll get a one-pager out in an hour for Procurement.

Thanks,
Mina
